data.description:
## Symptom

`AGENTS.md` names `scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py <change> --revision <sha>` as THE
sanctioned way to land a green Gerrit change, specifically to get revision-scoped submit
(409 instead of a silent submit when another session has uploaded a newer patch set).

In a non-interactive agent session the script exits **128** without submitting. It obtains
credentials by shelling out to `git credential fill`, which has no usable helper in that
context, so the call fails before any REST request is made.

## Impact

The documented path does not work for the exact caller it was written for. Every agent
session that follows `AGENTS.md` literally hits this and must improvise a raw `curl`
submit, which is how the revision-scoping safety property gets dropped in practice --
the improvised form is usually change-scoped `/submit`, which is precisely what the
script exists to prevent.

## Workaround currently in use

Fetch the admin password from SSM and POST the revision-scoped endpoint directly. Two
non-obvious details make the difference between working and failing:

- A bare `POST .../submit` returns **HTTP 400 "Expected JSON object"**. A body is
  required: `-d '{}'` with `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Gerrit prefixes REST responses with a 5-character `)]}'` guard that must be stripped
  (e.g. `tail -c +6`) before JSON parsing.

```sh
AP=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password \
      --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text)
SHA=$(curl -s -u "admin:$AP" ".../a/changes/$c/detail?o=CURRENT_REVISION" \
      | tail -c +6 | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['current_revision'])")
curl -s -X POST -u "admin:$AP" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' \
      ".../a/changes/$c/revisions/$SHA/submit"
```

## What is NOT yet known

Whether the right fix is to teach the script a non-interactive credential source (SSM,
or the same `http.extraHeader` Basic form used for `git push gerrit`), or to make it
reuse the checkout's configured Git credential helper the way `AGENTS.md` describes for
Gerrit REST calls. That choice should be made with evidence about which credential the
submit endpoint actually accepts, not by assumption.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause of the exit-128 failure is identified with evidence, not inference.
- [ ] `scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py` submits successfully from a non-interactive session
      with no TTY and no interactive credential helper.
- [ ] The script sends a JSON body, so it does not fail with 400 "Expected JSON object".
- [ ] The script strips Gerrit's `)]}'` response prefix before parsing.
- [ ] Revision-scoping is preserved: submitting a stale revision returns 409 rather than
      submitting, and there is a test covering that.
- [ ] A regression check exists that would fail if the script regains an interactive-only
      credential dependency.
data.title: scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py is unusable non-interactively: it shells git credential fill and exits 128
